card werk-mc-park-unpark  [open]
An un-park keeps a live process, and resumes a stopped one at once
why: A parked conversation whose process still runs has lost nothing, so a restart would only cost time. A conversation whose process was stopped must be back before the person types, so the resume starts at the click and not at the next message.

The page tells the server each time a conversation is parked or un-parked. Only the server knows whether the conversation's process still runs. To avoid a second process for one conversation, an un-park of a conversation with a live process changes nothing on the server. To avoid a wait at the next message, an un-park of a conversation with no live process and a known session starts a new process at once, and that process resumes the session (see #werk-resume). A conversation with no session yet starts nothing on un-park. Its first message starts a fresh process.

Example: conversations A and B. B has the session s-b. A has never sent a message.
1. B is parked. Its process still runs. The person clicks B in the '…' menu. B's chip comes back, and no process starts.
2. B is parked again and stays idle past the idle limit. The idle check kills its process (see #werk-mc-reap).
3. The person clicks B in the menu. The server starts a process at once, and it resumes s-b. The person types into a conversation that is already running.
4. A is un-parked. No process starts. A's first message starts a fresh process.

```
un-park B
  live process?  yes -> keep it, start nothing              (step 1)
                 no  -> session known?
                          yes -> start now, resume s-b      (step 3)
                          no  -> start nothing              (step 4)
```

    why not: The person types into a conversation that has no process. The message then waits while the process starts and the session loads, which is the slowest moment to wait.
